_readme: Tuple-form gateway policy vectors, generated by js/confidential/scripts/gen-gateway-tuple-vectors.ts.
SYNTHETIC ONLY: registers, key-provider payloads, evidence and signing keys are invented test inputs;
nothing here is a Google firmware value, an AnonRouter production pin or an Intel-signed quote.
Both languages must load, verify and signature-check these exact bytes to the recorded outcome.

loadCases.name: MIXED: platformKind with a legacy platform block
VTPM: a PCR allowlist is an unknown policy field
VTPM: a PCR field inside a tuple
gcp tuple must not carry a dstack osImageHash
gcp tuple must not carry a key provider
gcp tuple must not carry MRCONFIGID (it is required zero)
gcp app id must be a 32-byte verity root
phala tuple must not carry tdAttributes
phala tuple naming a non-KMS provider
phala key provider payload that is not JSON
release label outside the binding alphabet

verifyCases.name: gcp pilot: release A on firmware 1 over the retained socket
verifyCases.why: The only shape that passes: whole tuple, native DCAP, same-socket key, explicit pilot. The unqualified boot chain stays visible as an unmet advisory.

verifyCases.name: gcp pilot: release B on firmware 2
verifyCases.why: Tuples are OR: the second complete tuple matches on its own.

verifyCases.name: MIXED TUPLE: release B code on firmware 1
verifyCases.why: Every value is individually approved somewhere, but no single tuple holds them together.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: no single approved release tuple matches every measured value

verifyCases.name: MIXED TUPLE: release A label and verity root with release B compose
verifyCases.why: The release label, verity root and compose hash must come from the same tuple.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: no single approved release tuple matches every measured value

verifyCases.name: MIXED TUPLE: release A verity root on release B everything else
verifyCases.why: The verity root that RTMR1 commits to is part of the tuple.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: no single approved release tuple matches every measured value

verifyCases.name: WRONG PLATFORM: RTMR1 differs (another UKI)
verifyCases.why: A kernel, command line or verity root the tuple does not name fails even with everything else approved.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: no single approved release tuple matches every measured value

verifyCases.name: WRONG PLATFORM: TD attributes differ
verifyCases.why: The exact TD attributes are part of the tuple.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: no single approved release tuple matches every measured value

verifyCases.name: WRONG PLATFORM: MRCONFIGID set
verifyCases.why: Owner-supplied configuration registers must be zero.

verifyCases.name: WRONG PLATFORM: MROWNER set
verifyCases.why: Owner-supplied configuration registers must be zero.

verifyCases.name: RTMR3 EXTENDED
verifyCases.why: This guest measures no runtime events; any RTMR3 extension is unexplained code or configuration.

verifyCases.name: INSTANCE ID not derived from the boot key
verifyCases.why: The per-boot identity must be SHA-256 of the boot key the binding carries.

verifyCases.name: BOOT KEY not ed25519
verifyCases.why: The GCP boot key is Ed25519; another algorithm is a different protocol.

verifyCases.name: EXPIRED TUPLE
verifyCases.why: A tuple's own expiry ends acceptance even when every measurement matches.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: the matching release tuple is outside its validity window

verifyCases.name: NOT YET VALID TUPLE
verifyCases.why: A tuple cannot be used before its window opens.

expected.releaseTupleDetail: the matching release tuple is outside its validity window

verifyCases.name: WRONG KEY: another node's certificate on this socket
verifyCases.why: The quote binds a different per-boot TLS key than the connection presents.

verifyCases.name: WRONG KEY: no observed certificate
verifyCases.why: For GCP an unobserved certificate is a failure, never an advisory gap.

verifyCases.name: SEPARATE CONNECTION: matching SPKI not observed on the retained socket
verifyCases.why: A certificate seen on another connection may belong to another node behind the balancer.

verifyCases.name: NO PILOT OPT-IN
verifyCases.why: The native boot chain is unqualified, so an explicit caller acknowledgement is required.

verifyCases.name: NO NATIVE DCAP
verifyCases.why: Without an Intel chain verifier there is no substitute: GCP fails closed.

verifyCases.name: TCB not UpToDate
verifyCases.why: The signature can chain while the platform is out of date.

verifyCases.name: phala tuple form, full replay
verifyCases.why: The tuple form also serves the existing platform, with its full dstack replay and KMS provider.
